desc: A curated list of NLP resources focused on Transformer networks, attention mechanism, GPT, BERT, ChatGPT, LLMs, and transfer learning.

resources.name: PLMpapers
resources.desc: BERT (Transformer, transfer learning) has catalyzed research in pretrained language models (PLMs) and has sparked many extensions. This repo contains a list of papers on PLMs.

resources.name: What is XLNet and why it outperforms BERT
Visual Paper Summary: ALBERT (A Lite BERT)
The Annotated Transformer by Harvard NLP Group
resources.desc: Further reading to understand the "Attention is all you need" paper.

resources.name: Attention? Attention!
resources.desc: Attention guide by Lilian Weng from OpenAI.

resources.name: Making Transformer networks simpler and more efficient
resources.desc: FAIR released an all-attention layer to simplify the Transformer model and an adaptive attention span method to make it more efficient (reduce computation time and memory footprint).

resources.name: Transformers for software engineers
resources.desc: This post will be helpful to software engineers who are interested in learning ML models, especially anyone interested in Transformer interpretability. The post walk through a (mostly) complete implementation of a GPT-style Transformer, but the goal will not be running code; instead, they use the language of software engineering and programming to explain how these models work and articulate some of the perspectives they bring to them when doing interpretability work.

resources.name: Pathways Language Model (PaLM): Scaling to 540 Billion Parameters for Breakthrough Performance
resources.desc: PaLM is a dense decoder-only Transformer model trained with the Pathways system, which enabled Google to efficiently train a single model across multiple TPU v4 Pods. The example explaining a joke is remarkable. This shows that it can generate explicit explanations for scenarios that require a complex combination of multi-step logical inference, world knowledge, and deep language understanding.

resources.name: google-research/meliad
resources.desc: The Meliad library is collection of models which are being developed as part of ongoing Google research into various architectural improvements in deep learning. The library currently consists of several transformer variations, which explore ways in which the popular transformer architecture can be extended to better support language modeling over long sequences. The variations are Memorizing Transformer, Transformer with sliding window, Block-Recurrent Transformer, and more.

resources.name: The Secret Sauce behind 100K context window in LLMs: all tricks in one place
Improving Language Understanding with Unsupervised Learning
resources.desc: this is an overview of the original OpenAI GPT model.

resources.name: OpenGPT-2: We Replicated GPT-2 Because You Can Too
resources.desc: the authors trained a 1.5 billion parameter GPT-2 model on a similar sized text dataset and they reported results that can be compared with the original model.

resources.name: elyase/awesome-gpt3
resources.desc: A collection of demos and articles about the OpenAI GPT-3 API.

resources.name: GPT-Neo
resources.desc: Replicate a GPT-3 sized model and open source it for free. GPT-Neo is "an implementation of model parallel GPT2 & GPT3-like models, with the ability to scale up to full GPT3 sizes (and possibly more!), using the mesh-tensorflow library." [Code].

resources.name: GPT-4 Rumors From Silicon Valley
resources.desc: GPT-4 is almost ready. GPT-4 would be multimodal, accepting text, audio, image, and possibly video inputs. Release window: Dec - Feb. #hype

resources.desc: You can run BLOOM-176B/OPT-175B easily on a single machine, without performance degradation. If true, this could be a game changer in enabling people outside of big tech companies being able to use these LLMs.

resources.name: Teaching Small Language Models to Reason (paper)
resources.desc: They finetune a student model on the chain of thought (CoT) outputs generated by a larger teacher model. For example, the accuracy of T5 XXL on GSM8K improves from 8.11% to 21.99% when finetuned on PaLM-540B generated chains of thought.

resources.name: jeffhj/LM-reasoning

resources.name: lvwerra/TRL

resources.name: CarperAI/TRLX
resources.desc: Originated as a fork of TRL. It allows you to fine-tune Hugging Face language models (GPT2, GPT-NeoX based) up to 20B parameters using Reinforcement Learning. Brought to you by CarperAI (born at EleutherAI, an org part of StabilityAI family). CarperAI is developing production ready open-source RLHF tools. They have announced plans for the first open-source "instruction-tuned" LM.

resources.name: allenai/RL4LMs

resources.name: Evolution of representations in the Transformer
resources.desc: An accessible article that presents the insights of their EMNLP 2019 paper. They look at how the representations of individual tokens in Transformers trained with different objectives change.

resources.name: The dark secrets of BERT
resources.desc: This post probes fine-tuned BERT models for linguistic knowledge. In particular, the authors analyse how many self-attention patterns with some linguistic interpretation are actually used to solve downstream tasks. TL;DR: They are unable to find evidence that linguistically interpretable self-attention maps are crucial for downstream performance.

resources.name: A Visual Guide to Using BERT for the First Time

It works well for tasks like changing coding style, translating between programming languages, refactoring, and adding doc. For example, converts JSON into YAML, translates Python code to JavaScript, improve the runtime complexity of the function.

resources.name: How Much Better is OpenAI’s Newest GPT-3 Model?

resources.name: OpenAI rival Cohere launches language model API
resources.desc: Backed by AI experts, they aims to bring Google-quality predictive language to the masses. Aidan Gomez co-wrote a seminal 2017 paper at Google Brain that invented a concept known as "Transformers".

resources.name: Startups competing with OpenAI's GPT-3 all need to solve the same problems
resources.desc: Last year, two startups released their own proprietary text-generation APIs. AI21 Labs, launched its 178-billion-parameter Jurassic-1 in Aug 2021, and Cohere, released a range of models. Cohere hasn't disclosed how many parameters its models contain. ... There are other up-and-coming startups looking to solve the same issues. Anthropic, the AI safety and research company started by a group of ex-OpenAI employees. Several researchers have left Google Brain to join two new ventures started by their colleagues. One outfit is named Character.ai, and the other Persimmon Labs.

resources.name: The Next Generation Of Large Language Models
resources.desc: It highlights 3 emerging areas: 1) models that can generate their own training data to improve themselves, 2) models that can fact-check themselves, and 3) massive sparse expert models.

resources.name: GPT-4 analysis and predictions
resources.desc: Somehow related, in "Bing Chat is blatantly, aggressively misaligned" post, Gwern think how Bing Chat/Sydney can be so different from ChatGPT and his hypothesis: "Sydney is not a RLHF trained GPT-3 model but a GPT-4 model developed in a hurry". Some have also argued that Sydney performs better on reasoning tasks than ChatGPT/GPT-3.5 and it may be GPT-4.

Note that Karpathy's bottom up approach and fast.ai teaching style work well together. (FYI, fast.ai has both top-down ("part 1") and bottom-up ("part 2") approach.)

Trials and tribulations of OPT-175B training by Susan Zhang at Meta
resources.desc: In this talk, they walk through the development lifecycle of OPT-175B, covering infrastructure and training convergence challenges faced at scale, along with methods of addressing these issues going forward. Amazing that they managed to pull off such a feat. Key takeaway: data matters a lot! Super deep understanding of neural networks nuts&bolts (LR, SGD, etc.) and engineering. Even more than usual time spend staring at the loss curves. Understanding the Chinchilla's scaling law of how the new architecture/algorithms works as you scale up. [LLM training log]
